confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on two web searches. One returned the RBA rate and the other returned Lisbon price data, mainly Numbeo figures (as of about June 2026) reproduced on Expatica, plus travel guides. I converted euro prices to USD at roughly 1.16 USD per EUR, which is my assumption and not a sourced rate. Numbeo shows a cappuccino at about €2.40, a draught beer at about €3.13, an inexpensive meal at about €13.50 and a three-course dinner for two at about €52. Cocktail and wine were not directly sourced from an index. I took cocktails from guide ranges of €9-12 in nightlife areas, and wine as a restaurant glass of about €4.5-5. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge, not from live listings, and July is peak season, so they are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Lisbon is priced near the middle of Western Europe: cheaper than Paris or Amsterdam, and above Porto and other Portuguese cities. Tourist-area prices run higher than the Numbeo averages.
